The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers saw no failure, but their stored monthly spend totals stopped matching their purchases
Why, in plain words: A code change stopped the shop from updating each shopper's saved spending-this-month figure when they bought something, while the parts of the shop that show and check that figure still use the saved copy.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 7d 0h 0m 32s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none so far {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: refused to act on a suspected cause - nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken - recommends: roll io-shop back
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #555 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers saw no failure, but their stored monthly spend totals stopped matching their purchases
Incident: SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile on io-shop
Date: Nov 04, 2026, 04:09 UTC, not back to normal by Nov 11, 2026, 04:09:32 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:43:54 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 04:09:04 UTC
Ended by: Argus: recommended to a person, Nov 11, 2026, 04:09:32 UTC - roll io-shop back

Summary
The service broke at Nov 04, 04:09 UTC and was not back to normal by Nov 11, 04:09:32 UTC, at least 7 days 32 seconds later. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. A code change stopped the shop from updating each shopper's saved spending-this-month figure when they bought something, while the parts of the shop that show and check that figure still use the saved copy. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #555, for a person to review and merge. It was written against main, which does not contain the revision that ran: merged, it changes what runs only once a deploy carries it. Argus recommends this and did not take it: roll io-shop back. The month totals already saved short stayed wrong, and each new purchase this month could leave them further short, so monthly statements and spend summaries could keep showing shoppers figures that disagree with what they bought; a shopper routed through the month-deriving write path could see the same drift even after a rollback.

Impact
at least 7d 0h 0m 32s - since onset, still not back to normal
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
none so far - customer loss (estimated)
AL1: What the alert found: 240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile with the purchases behind them. The widest is short by 1,297.31, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at 2026-11-04T04:09:00Z. Found by the spend-integrity check, which runs every 7 days, so the fault is up to that old.

Root cause and contributing factors
The change took the total_this_month_cents update out of record_purchase, and the other write path, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, does not move it either, so every current-month purchase written afterwards left the stored month total short by its price. The field still sits on the account and is still used: render_monthly_statement and _compared_with_usual read it, the_mean_purchase_this_month and average_spend_per_item_this_month divide it by a count of purchases, and reconcile_monthly_totals compares it with the sum of the current-month purchases.
Causal chain
symptom No one using the shop was seen to hit a failure. What was seen instead: the spend-integrity check found that shoppers' stored month totals did not match the purchases behind them.
  Evidence:
    AL1
why 1 Purchases written after the onset were stored without moving the account's month total. At the revision that ran, record_purchase and record_purchase_deriving_the_month both append the purchase and add only to total_cents, so total_this_month_cents stayed where it was whichever path the purchase took.
  Evidence:
    S1 src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py at 26f1d7e
why 2 That write path arrived with deploy P2 at 04:08:18 UTC, which removed the month-total update from record_purchase. All 3 replicas were running that revision as of Nov 11, 04:09:19 UTC.
  Evidence:
    P2 04:08:18 UTC deploy 26f1d7e by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    D1 Deployment of revision 26f1d7e to io-shop, compared against 4c810f2 - the revision deployed before it.
    T9 Nov 11 04:09:19 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision 26f1d7e, deployed at Nov 04 04:08:18
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy P1: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at 04:09 UTC, after P2 at 04:08:18 UTC, so the service did no harm while P1's revision was running.
      AL1
      P1 00:08:18 UTC deploy 4c810f2 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
      P2
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour 1 minute before Nov 04 04:10.
      T13
why 3 The change stopped writing total_this_month_cents, but the field was kept and the code around it still uses the stored value: the monthly statement reads it in render_monthly_statement and _compared_with_usual, the_mean_purchase_this_month and average_spend_per_item_this_month divide it by a count of purchases, and reconcile_monthly_totals compares it with the sum of the current-month purchases.
  Evidence:
    D1
    S1
    U1 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:650, in the_mean_purchase_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought)
    U2 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:882, in _compared_with_usual: reads it: this_month_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
    U3 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:918, in render_monthly_statement: reads it: month_total_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
    U4 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:109, in reconcile_monthly_totals: compares it with _bought_this_month(account), where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
    U6 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, in average_spend_per_item_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)
Contributing factors
- Month-total drift was watched only by the spend-integrity check, which runs every 7 days. The module itself says nothing in the write path notices when a total and the purchases disagree. (AI-4)
- The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it. (AI-5)
- By Code-Fix's reading, the test file at the deployed revision holds a test that pins record_purchase adding to the month total, which the deployed code no longer does. No test run before the deploy was seen. (AI-6)
- No review was seen that checked who still uses total_this_month_cents before the change stopped writing it, even though the module's own docstring warns that a write moving one copy and not the other leaves two answers. (AI-7)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | Revision 26f1d7e, deployed at 04:08:18 UTC, changed record_purchase in purchase_ledger.py so it no longer maintains the stored month total. Since then accounts have been written with totals that disagree with their purchase history. Serving did not change, so every series stayed flat. The spend-integrity check reports the oldest wrong record at 04:09 UTC. | 0.60 | never tried: nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken
C2 | The deployment of 26f1d7e shipped faulty code in purchase_ledger.py that stopped maintaining the month total. This is the same change as the first hypothesis, read as a plain bad deployment. | 0.30 | never tried: nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken

Trigger
Suspected, not confirmed: io-shop was deployed from 4c810f2 to 26f1d7e at 04:08:18 UTC, by kuki.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
 | Nov 11 04:09:32 | Refused to act on C1 - nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken | Argus | nothing to put back | not taken
 | Nov 11 04:12:40 | Proposed a fix: PR #555 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 04:09 UTC. SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile fired at Nov 11, 2026, 04:08:59 UTC, 6 days 23 hours 59 minutes 59 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #555 | open
AI-2 | Roll io-shop back | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Correct the stored month totals of the affected accounts once a fixed or rolled-back revision is running, for example with the repair script Code-Fix proposed: run it with --apply on an account export taken in the same month, then load the corrected accounts back. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Run the spend-integrity reconciliation (reconcile_monthly_totals) much more often than its current cadence. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the on-call paging rotation for io-shop. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Make the io-shop deploy pipeline require the test suite to pass before any revision is deployed. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Add a review checklist rule: a change that stops writing a stored field must list every user of that field and show each one no longer depends on it. | process | unassigned | - | open
Argus declined to act, and recommends: roll io-shop back

Lessons learned
What went well
- 20 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision 26f1d7e, deployed at Nov 04 04:08:18.
- 27 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 26f1d7e changed.
- 28 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour 1 minute before Nov 04 04:10.
- 33 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus refused to act on C1 - nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken.
- 3 minutes 41 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #555.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Supporting information

The fix it proposed: PR #555 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/555) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 00:08:18 UTC deploy 4c810f2 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
P2 | 04:08:18 UTC deploy 26f1d7e by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
Flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
Not read.
What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision 26f1d7e to io-shop, compared against 4c810f2 - the revision deployed before it.
modified src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py
  @@ -28,26 +28,23 @@
   
   
   def record_purchase(account: Account, purchase: Purchase) -> Account:
  -    """The account with this purchase written into it, and both totals moved.
  +    """The account with this purchase written into it, and its total moved.
   
  -    How a purchase has always been recorded. Each total is added to rather than
  -    worked out again: the account already carries what has been spent, and a sale
  -    changes it by exactly the price of the thing sold.
  +    How a purchase is recorded. The lifetime total is added to rather than worked
  +    out again: the account already carries what has been spent, and a sale changes
  +    it by exactly the price of the thing sold.
   
  -    The month is the part worth reading twice. A purchase counts towards the
  -    month's total only if it falls in the month being counted, so that addition is
  -    conditional where the lifetime one is not - and a shopper backfilling an older
  -    order leaves this month's figure exactly where it was.
  +    The month is no longer carried. Every purchase says whether it falls in the
  +    current month, so what a shopper has spent this month adds up from the history
  +    whenever anybody wants it - exactly as the lifetime average is derived from the
  +    purchases rather than read off the account. A second copy of a figure the
  +    purchases already hold is a copy that has to be kept in step, and the cheapest
  +    way to keep it in step is not to keep it.
       """
       return replace(
           account,
           purchases=(*account.purchases, purchase),
  -        total_cents=account.total_cents + purchase.price_cents,
  -        total_this_month_cents=(
  -            account.total_this_month_cents + purchase.price_cents
  -            if purchase.in_current_month
  -            else account.total_this_month_cents
  -        )
  +        total_cents=account.total_cents + purchase.price_cents
       )
   
   
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | Which code each claim is about. The revision that ran, 26f1d7e…, is not in main's history, so I have not read it. What it did comes from the investigation: it took the total_this_month_cents update out of record_purchase. Everything else below is about main.

The fault on main. In src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py on main, record_purchase still moves the month total. The same file also has a second write path, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, which record_a_purchase picks when derive_the_month is true. That path appends the purchase and adds to total_cents, but leaves total_this_month_cents at whatever the account already held. So main contains the same fault the deployed revision shipped, behind a flag: any purchase written through that path leaves the stored month total out of step with the account's purchases. That is the mismatch the investigation's alert reports.

The fix (src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py). record_purchase_deriving_the_month now writes total_this_month_cents as the sum of price_cents over the account's purchases marked in_current_month, counting the new purchase. A side effect: an account whose stored month had already drifted is put right the next time it is written through this path. record_purchase is unchanged and keeps adding to the total it receives; the existing test test_the_month_is_added_to_what_was_already_spent_in_it pins that. No function signature in the file changed.

Tests (tests/io_shop/test_purchase_ledger.py).
• The deriving path moves the month total for a purchase in this month.
• It leaves the total alone for a purchase from an earlier month.
• It writes the month as its purchases add up, even when the account arrived with a total that had drifted.
• After a sequence of writes with either value of derive_the_month, reconcile_monthly_totals reports nothing that disagrees.

Against current main, the first, third and fourth tests should fail: the deriving path leaves the total at its old value. Nothing has run these tests or the fix.

Repair (src/io_shop/repair_monthly_totals.py). This is a one-off script, and it has not been run. A person has to run it against production data. It reads accounts from a JSON export and uses reconcile_monthly_totals to pick the accounts it reports. For each of those it sets total_this_month_cents to the sum of that account's current-month purchase prices, changing no other field. Each correction is printed with the old value, the new value and the oldest affected purchase.
• By default it only reports. It writes the corrected accounts to the output file only when --apply and --output are given.
• The script does not load from or write to any store: exporting the accounts to the file and loading the corrected ones back is the operator's job.
• in_current_month comes from the export, so the export should be taken in the same month the script is run.
What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired

The document, by field:
overview: A code change on io-shop stopped the shop from updating each shopper's saved spending-this-month figure when they bought something. Shoppers saw no errors, but for shoppers who made purchases after the change, the saved monthly spend totals stopped matching what they had actually bought. This matters because the parts of the shop that show and check that figure still read the saved copy. The problem has gone on for {duration}. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus did not roll io-shop back itself, because nothing could show within Argus's waiting time whether a rollback would fix the problem. Instead, it recommends rolling io-shop back. Argus also opened a proposed fix, PR #555, as a draft. That fix has not been run, so none of its changes have happened yet.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
